topics.title: HTML Performance Best Practices
topics.summary: Make pages load and render fast: small HTML, optimised media, non-blocking scripts and good Core Web Vitals.
topics.description:
Fast pages rank better, convert better and work on slow phones. Much of the speed is decided by your HTML.

### What users feel - Core Web Vitals
| Metric | Meaning | Target |
|---|---|---|
| **LCP** Largest Contentful Paint | When the main content appears | ≤ 2.5 s |
| **INP** Interaction to Next Paint | Responsiveness to input | ≤ 200 ms |
| **CLS** Cumulative Layout Shift | Visual stability | ≤ 0.1 |

### Checklist
1. **Images**: right size, modern format (WebP/AVIF), `srcset`, `width`/`height`, `loading="lazy"` below the fold, `fetchpriority="high"` on the hero.
2. **Scripts**: `defer`/`async`, remove unused JS, avoid huge libraries for tiny jobs.
3. **CSS**: small critical CSS first, avoid `@import` chains, remove unused rules.
4. **Fonts**: `font-display: swap`, preload the key font, subset.
5. **Resource hints**: `preconnect` to key origins, `preload` only critical files.
6. **Third parties**: audit each one - ads and widgets are the usual culprits.
7. **DOM size**: avoid thousands of nested nodes; use semantic simple markup.
8. **Network**: HTTPS + HTTP/2/3, gzip/Brotli, caching headers, CDN.
9. **Media**: `preload="none"` for videos, poster images, no autoplay.
10. **Layout shift**: reserve space for images, ads and embeds.

### Measure it
Lighthouse, PageSpeed Insights, WebPageTest and DevTools **Performance** + **Network** tabs. Test on a throttled mobile profile, not just your fast laptop.

### The simplest win
Every byte you do not send is free. Delete what you do not need.
keyPoints: Core Web Vitals: LCP, INP and CLS.
Optimise images: format, size, srcset, lazy loading, dimensions.
Never block rendering with scripts - use defer/async.
Preload only critical resources; preconnect to key origins.
Measure with Lighthouse and DevTools on mobile settings.

examples.title: A performance-minded page

interview.a: Google metrics for user experience: LCP (loading), INP (interactivity) and CLS (visual stability).

interview.q: Name HTML-level ways to improve load speed.
interview.a: Optimise and lazy-load images with dimensions, defer scripts, preload critical assets, preconnect to origins, reduce DOM size and third parties.

interview.q: What causes layout shift and how do you prevent it?
interview.a: Content that loads without reserved space (images, ads, fonts). Set width/height or aspect-ratio and reserve slots.

topics.title: HTML Security: XSS, sandbox, noopener & CSP
topics.summary: Escape untrusted data, restrict iframes, protect links and know what Content Security Policy does.
topics.description:
HTML is where many web attacks land. Know the basics.

### 1. XSS (Cross-Site Scripting)
Attacker-supplied text is inserted into the page and runs as script.
- **Never** put untrusted data in `innerHTML`, `document.write` or inline event handlers.
- Use `textContent` or escape: `<` → `<`, `&` → `&`, `"` → `"`.
- Sanitise rich text with a library (DOMPurify) or the Sanitizer API.
- Escape for the context: HTML body, attribute, URL and JS all differ.

### 2. Safe links
`target="_blank"` without `rel="noopener"` lets the new page access `window.opener` (reverse tabnabbing). Modern browsers default to noopener, but add it for clarity. Also validate user-supplied URLs - reject `javascript:`.

### 3. iframe sandbox
```html
<iframe src="https://thirdparty.example" sandbox="allow-scripts" title="Widget"></iframe>
```
An empty `sandbox` blocks scripts, forms, popups and same-origin access. Add back only what is needed: `allow-scripts`, `allow-forms`, `allow-same-origin` (never together with allow-scripts for untrusted code).

### 4. Content Security Policy
A header (or `<meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy">`) that whitelists sources of scripts, styles and frames:
```
Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'
```

### 5. Other
- Subresource Integrity: `<script integrity="sha384-..." crossorigin>` for CDN files.
- `autocomplete` tokens, `type="password"`, HTTPS everywhere, no secrets in HTML or comments.
- `<form>` POST with CSRF tokens (server-side).
keyPoints: Escape or use textContent for untrusted data; avoid innerHTML.
Use rel="noopener" with target="_blank".
sandbox restricts iframes; grant minimal permissions.
CSP limits where scripts and frames can come from.
Use SRI for third-party scripts and HTTPS everywhere.
pitfalls: Using sandbox="allow-scripts allow-same-origin" on untrusted pages - the sandbox can be removed.
Putting API secrets in client-side HTML or comments.

interview.q: What is XSS and how do you prevent it?
interview.a: Injecting malicious script into a page via untrusted input. Prevent by escaping/sanitising output, using textContent, and a Content Security Policy.

interview.q: What does the iframe sandbox attribute do?
interview.a: It applies extra restrictions to the framed content (no scripts, forms, popups, same-origin) unless specific allow-* tokens are given.

interview.q: Why add rel="noopener" to target="_blank" links?
interview.a: To stop the opened page from accessing window.opener and redirecting your original tab (reverse tabnabbing).

topics.title: HTML Best Practices & Common Mistakes
topics.summary: A practical checklist for clean, valid, maintainable and accessible HTML.
topics.description:
Good HTML is invisible - it just works everywhere. Use this checklist before shipping. ### Structure & syntax - Start with ``, `lang`, `charset` and viewport meta. - Use **lowercase** tags and attributes, always quote attribute values. - Close all non-void elements and nest properly. - One `

`, no skipped heading levels, one `
`. - Validate with the W3C validator (validator.w3.org). ### Semantics - Prefer semantic elements over div/span; buttons for actions, links for navigation. - Use lists for lists, tables for data, ``, `
keyPoints: Validate your HTML and keep it semantic.
Lowercase tags, quoted attributes, properly nested elements.
Separate structure (HTML), style (CSS), behaviour (JS).
Provide alt, labels and descriptive links.
Never use HTML elements purely for presentation.
pitfalls: Div soup and class names like .red-box.
Using tables for layout or br for spacing.

interview.q: How do you check that HTML is valid?
interview.a: Use the W3C Markup Validator or browser DevTools/linters (HTMLHint, ESLint plugins).

interview.q: Why separate HTML, CSS and JS?
interview.a: Better maintainability, caching, reuse and smaller pages; each language does one job.

interview.q: Why not use br for spacing?
interview.a: br means a line break in text; spacing is presentation and should be done with CSS margin/padding.

topics.title: Project: A Complete Landing Page
topics.summary: Put everything together: semantic layout, hero, about with skills, services figures, article, audio and contact form.
topics.description:
This is the course project rebuilt as a standalone page. It shows how the topics fit together in one document - no external files needed.

### Page plan
| Section | Elements used |
|---|---|
| Header | `header`, `nav`, `ul`, logo emoji |
| Hero | `main`, `h1`, `p`, `button`, `a`, `figure` |
| About | `section`, `h2`, `p`, `label` + `meter`/`progress` |
| Services | `section`, `figure` + `figcaption` |
| Blog article | `article`, `header`, nested `section`, `h3`, `strong`, `em` |
| Podcast | `audio` with controls |
| Links | list of `a` |
| Contact | `form` with label/input/textarea, optional map iframe |
| Footer | `footer`, `©` entity |

### Steps to build it
1. Start with the boilerplate (doctype, lang, charset, viewport, title, description).
2. Write the **semantic skeleton** first - no styling.
3. Fill in content: headings in order, real text, descriptive alt.
4. Add forms with labels and names.
5. Add minimal CSS for layout and readability.
6. Validate, test with keyboard only, check on a narrow window.

### Hosting
Static sites can be hosted free on Netlify, Vercel, GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages - drag the folder or connect a repo.

### Final SEO pass
Title and description, one h1, alt texts, Open Graph tags, favicon, canonical URL, fast images.

### Ideas to extend
Add a sticky nav, dark mode with CSS variables, a details FAQ, structured data and lazy-loaded gallery.
keyPoints: Plan sections first, then pick semantic elements.
Write HTML structure before CSS.
Every image has alt and dimensions; every input has a label.
Test with keyboard and a narrow viewport.
Static sites can be hosted free (Netlify, GitHub Pages).
pitfalls: Starting with styling before the structure is correct.
Using a div for every section.
Forgetting to test the form and links.

topics.title: Interview Questions: Fundamentals
topics.summary: The most common beginner/intermediate HTML interview questions with crisp answers.
topics.description:
Use this page as a **rapid-fire revision sheet**. Say the answer in one or two sentences, then give a tiny example. ### Basics | Question | Short answer | |---|---| | What is HTML? | HyperText Markup Language - the standard markup that structures web pages. | | Tag vs element? | Tag is the markup (`

`); element = opening tag + content + closing tag. | | What is the DOCTYPE? | Declaration that triggers standards mode (HTML5: ``). | | Void elements? | Elements without content/closing tag: br, hr, img, input, meta, link. | | Block vs inline? | Block starts a new line and takes the full width; inline flows in text. | | id vs class? | id unique, class reusable. | | div vs span? | Block generic container vs inline generic container. | | HTML vs HTML5? | HTML5 added semantic tags, audio/video, canvas, storage, forms, APIs and removed presentational tags. | | Is HTML case sensitive? | Not for tag and attribute names; lowercase is the convention. | ### Text, links, images | Question | Short answer | |---|---| | How many h1? | One main h1 per page is best practice. | | strong vs b? | strong = importance (semantic), b = visual boldness. | | Why alt? | Accessibility, fallback, SEO. | | _blank? | Opens in a new tab; add rel="noopener". | | mailto / tel? | Links that open email client / phone dialer. | | Absolute vs relative URL? | Full address vs resolved from the current location. | ### Forms and tables | Question | Short answer | |---|---| | GET vs POST? | URL query vs request body. | | readonly vs disabled? | readonly is submitted; disabled is not. | | Radio vs checkbox? | One of many vs many. | | select vs datalist? | Forced choice vs suggestions. | | thead/tbody/tfoot? | Group header, body, footer rows. | | colspan/rowspan? | Merge cells horizontally/vertically. | | th vs td? | Header cell vs data cell. |
keyPoints: Answer in one sentence, then give a mini example.
Know the pairs: tag/element, block/inline, id/class, div/span.
Know form pairs: GET/POST, readonly/disabled, select/datalist.
Mention accessibility and semantics where relevant.
pitfalls: Saying HTML is a programming language.

interview.q: What is the difference between HTML and HTML5?
interview.a: HTML5 is the current standard that added semantic elements, native audio/video, canvas, SVG, new form controls, storage and many APIs, and dropped presentational tags.

interview.q: What are semantic elements? Give examples.
interview.a: Elements whose names describe their meaning: header, nav, main, article, section, aside, footer, figure.

interview.q: How do you make a link open an email client?
Why is the alt attribute required on images?
interview.a: It supplies a text alternative for screen readers, failed loads and search engines.

topics.title: Interview Questions: Advanced & Scenario-Based
topics.summary: Deeper questions about performance, accessibility, SEO, APIs and real-world scenarios.
topics.description:
These questions separate good candidates from great ones. Practise answering them with a reason and a trade-off.

### Performance and loading
| Question | Short answer |
|---|---|
| defer vs async? | Both download in parallel; defer runs after parsing in order, async runs ASAP in any order. |
| How to speed up a page? | Optimise images, lazy load, defer JS, preload critical assets, reduce DOM/CSS/JS, CDN and caching. |
| preload vs prefetch? | Current page high priority vs future navigation low priority. |
| What is critical rendering path? | HTML → DOM, CSS → CSSOM, combined into render tree, layout, paint. |
| What causes CLS? | Images/ads/fonts without reserved space. |

### Accessibility and SEO
| Question | Short answer |
|---|---|
| First rule of ARIA? | Use native HTML before ARIA. |
| How to make a custom button accessible? | Prefer button; else role, tabindex="0", key handlers, name, focus style. |
| How to make forms accessible? | Labels, fieldset/legend, error messages linked with aria-describedby, correct types. |
| SEO tags? | title, meta description, canonical, h1, alt, Open Graph, structured data, robots. |

### HTML5 APIs
| Question | Short answer |
|---|---|
| localStorage vs cookies? | 5 MB, client-only, persistent vs 4 KB, sent with each request. |
| Web workers? | Background threads without DOM access using postMessage. |
| What is Shadow DOM? | Encapsulated DOM/CSS subtree for web components. |
| canvas vs SVG? | Pixels vs vectors. |
| How does drag and drop work? | draggable + dragstart, dragover (preventDefault), drop. |

### Scenario questions
- **"A page looks tiny on mobile."** → missing viewport meta.
- **"Image causes layout jump."** → missing width/height.
- **"Link opens but the opener tab is hijacked."** → add rel="noopener".
- **"Form submits but the server gets nothing for a field."** → missing name attribute or disabled.
- **"Emoji shows as ???"** → missing UTF-8 charset.
- **"Two elements react to one label."** → duplicate ids.
keyPoints: Explain the critical rendering path in one breath.
Know async/defer, preload/prefetch, localStorage/cookies.
Have a debugging answer for common scenarios.
Always connect answers to accessibility and performance.
pitfalls: Memorising answers without understanding the reason.

examples.title: Scenario: a form field is not submitted
examples.html: Submit to see what is sent.
examples.explanation: Only inputs with a name and not disabled appear.

interview.a: The browser parses HTML into the DOM and CSS into the CSSOM, combines them into a render tree, computes layout and paints. Blocking CSS/JS delays it.

interview.q: How would you make a div act as a button accessibly?
interview.a: Better to use a real button. Otherwise add role="button", tabindex="0", handle Enter/Space keys, give a name and visible focus.

interview.q: Why might a form field not reach the server?
interview.a: It has no name, is disabled, is outside the form without the form attribute, or is an unchecked checkbox/radio.

interview.q: How can you prevent layout shift from images?
interview.a: Set width and height attributes (or CSS aspect-ratio) so space is reserved before loading.
